title: Introduction to LLMs
subtitle: What large language models are and what they can do

content.text: A Large Language Model (LLM) is a neural network trained on vast text corpora to predict the next token. Through this training they develop impressive language and reasoning abilities.

content.definition: The basic unit an LLM processes. A token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words in English.
The maximum number of tokens an LLM can process at once — including both the input and output.

content.code:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var

message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain what an LLM is in one paragraph."}]
)

print(message.content[0].text)

content.text: LLMs are probabilistic. The same prompt can give different outputs. Control this with temperature (0 = deterministic).

questions.question: What is a token in the context of LLMs?
options: The basic unit of text processing (roughly 4 characters)
questions.explanation: Tokens are the sub-word units LLMs process. English averages about 0.75 words per token.

faq.a: No intrinsic memory. You must include prior turns in the context window (messages array) to give the model conversation history.
